How much does a quote "A delayed game is eventually good, but a rushed game is forever bad." hold up today? What are some games that defy the quote?
It's basically the A, B, C, A+B= Not C, C+B=Not A, A+C=Not B, A+B+C does not exist thing I've seen in many, many other graphs.
Let's see...all those games with bad launches and eventual fixes vs Duke Nukem Forever.

Games are now a service, more than a fixed product, so there's a chance bad games could become good. One example is FFXIV. The game was so bad they literally ended the world in a cataclysm and rebuilt it from the ground up as a post-apocalyptic scenario.

Arkham Knight was delayed for over 8 months (not including the delay after it was pulled from sale) and despite that the PC developer literally gave up trying to fix it, saying they didn't want to break it more by accident.

I want to say Diablo 3 defies that quote, but in the minds of many people it doesn't. If you went out on a leap of faith and allowed the expansion to woo you, the game is amazing. Really truly completely fixed from launch.

However, so many people have such a terrible impression of Diablo 3 because of it's launch state, they are never coming back no matter what they hear.
While I thouroghly enjoyed Diablo 3 (only played after RoS), it satisfies a much different itch than its predecessors, and I can see why that rubs some fans the wrong way.

That may just come from how sequels work these days. Once upon a time sequels had the potential to be wildly different after each iteration. Actually now that I think about it, that was mostly the case in the late 90's.

I mean, you look at the huge franchises from the 80's and early 90's, and sequels were basically more of the exact same pounded out in around a year or two, sometimes with an expansion pack released after 3 to 6 months. Look at the entirety of the Wizardry series, right up until the last one that went full 3D. Or the Might & Magic series up until 6 came out in the mid 90's. Or Doom, to Ultimate Doom, to Doom 2, to the many other official and unofficial expansion packs. Same thing goes for Quake. Even Command & Conquer stayed mostly the same from Command & Conquer to Red Alert to Tiberium Sun.

But yeah, something about the late 90's, sequels went fucknuts.

Quake 2 was a huge departure from Quake. Might & Magic 6 totally broke the mold. Even Diablo 2 was a really different game from Diablo, compared to the decidedly incremental changes most sequels made on the formula.

I guess the late 90's was a weird time where companies were drowning in money, and had tons of time and resources to try to reinvent the wheel. Of course now they are mostly back to yearly installments and rushed out expansion packs (DLC) again.
